flash driver: provide setup for selecting cbfses from fmap The offset needn't be added at all times (in fact, just for the first two accesses), so we look for out of bounds conditions to check when it's required to add the offset and when it needn't be. This approach works because the CBFS images' offsets are larger than their own size. This restriction (and this imprecise approach) will be lifted in follow-up commits. BUG=chromium:445938 BRANCH=tot TEST=none Change-Id: I3f60a3a66ed8d6654be5bed1ca1f4b4b2cd5b8d7 Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/306600 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@chromium.org>

Support fetching EC firmware from CBFS-formatted FW_MAIN_* With MULTIPLE_CBFS_INSTANCES enabled, EC firmware and hashes come from CBFS instead of its separate fmap region and an indexes FW_MAIN_*, respectively. This is currently implemented as a fallback option when the normal "indexed" approach fails. Doesn't hurt to add another try then, and due to details in the CBFS format, it's guaranteed that this fallback is taken with MULTIPLE_CBFS_INSTANCES. Once that configuration is in operation, the old code path can be taken out. BUG=chromium:445938 BRANCH=tot TEST=none Change-Id: I5ac553de3f5dcd0bf59cc1e91aa2e7eed6c23e6e Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/306602 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@chromium.org>

util: signer: cr50: use full flash addresses instead of segment addresses The code mixes up using of full flash addresses and flash segment addresses (full address divided by 16). The vast majority of uses in fact requires full addresses, but all definitions are using segment addresses. This patch converts definitions to full addresses, which improves overall code readability. CHROMIUM: Allow disk-based swap files By default, the Chromium OS kernel allows swapping only to zram devices (for details see commit acc9d0ae7b). But using disk-based files as swap devices is required for machines that have a tiny amount of memory. This patch introduces a kernel config option (CONFIG_DISK_BASED_SWAP) and a sysctl variable (disk_based_swap) to allow disk-based files as swap devices. To minimize exposure, CONFIG_DISK_BASED_SWAP is set to N and disk_based_swap is set to 0 by default. BUG=b:25356904 TEST=Wrote a test program that grows incrementally to a size larger than system memory, causing paging and swapping. Verfied that data pages of the test program were written to the disk-based swap device. Change-Id: I6cfc1ba921d6f1a9a8fdceba1e387e0eedafca89 Signed-off-by: Saied Kazemi <saied@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/311795 Reviewed-by: Aditya Kali <adityakali@google.com> Reviewed-by: Filipe Brandenburger <filbranden@chromium.org>

edid: Use a better mode for 640x480 The hardcoded clock value for 640x480 was 25.175 MHz. That's a valid clock to use, but is quite hard to make a non-jittery clock from PLLs. It's much easier to make 25.200 MHz, so let's do that. The difference between the two modes is 59.9 Hz vs. 60 Hz and it seems better to make a non-jittery 60 Hz rather than a very jittery 59.9 Hz. CHROMIUM: iio: cros_ec: Relax sampling frequency before suspending. If an application set a tight sampling frequency, given the interrupt use is a wakup source, suspend will not happen: the kernel will receive a wake up interrupt and will cancel the suspend process. Given cros_ec sensors type is non wake up, add prepare/complete calls to set 1s sampling period just before suspend, to ensure the sensor hub will not be a source of interrupt during the suspend process. BUG=b:25425420 TEST=With this change, pass the CTS test DeviceSuspendTestActivity::testAccelBatchingInApSuspendZeroReportLatency reliabely.
